capabilities.blurb: New seat: Zeus, the Chief of Staff. Give him a task that spans several seats and he plans it, delegates each part, and merges the results. When no seat fits he proposes a single-use specialist, which starts only after you approve it.

The security audit now checks your permission ALLOW rules too -- rules that silently never match, and ones that let any script run or any file leave the machine without asking -- and can show you the warning Claude Code flashes at startup that is gone before you can read it.
New /harness-fix: approve, decline or defer a review's fix options.
New /harness-heal (propose-only): checks a pre-approved fix's preconditions before you run it.
New /harness-review: turns each failed scheduled run into a root cause and ranked fixes you can choose from.
Record a dated commitment with scripts/commitments.py and it surfaces at the start of every session once it is due within a week or overdue -- so review dates stop expiring quietly.
Tells you at session start when a scheduled job has quietly stopped running -- or starts every day and dies halfway -- instead of letting it stay dead for days unnoticed.
Files you've said must change together are checked at the end of each turn: touch one without the other and the turn can't end until the co-change is done or explained.
When you save a memory, it now checks you'd actually find it again -- by searching with the file's own description -- and won't let the turn end until it would. No index line needed.
The rule that applies to a file now shows up before you write to it, so a "remember to also update X" is in front of you at the moment you act, once per session.
The one shared definition of 'would I find this memory?', so the end-of-turn check and the full report can never disagree.
Failed scheduled runs are now queued for /harness-review automatically.
The read-time injection scan now pauses on suspicious external mail; re-reading it in the same session goes through.
A config file that the scanner flags as possibly poisoned now needs your confirmation before it is written; an agent simply retrying is not enough.
Your session now opens by telling you when /harness-review has a fix proposal waiting for your decision, and says nothing when there isn't one.
A red circle now means one thing: unverified. Whether something is good or bad is shown with a tick, a warning sign or a cross instead.

New: Agent Org. A live pane beside the conversation and a local dashboard show every agent running, every tool call and every safety gate as it happens, and Zeus, a Chief of Staff, plans multi-part tasks and hands each part to the right seat. Specialists he proposes run only after you approve them. Say yes to turn it on (needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later).
python scripts/commitments.py --add "..." --date YYYY-MM-DD records a dated commitment; --due lists what is overdue or due this week; --done closes one.
Removes the duplicate edges that re-running the graph extractor builds up, so counts and retrieval stop being skewed by repeats.
The harness watch now spots failures that never reached the error log, risky unattended-run audits, and a review queue nobody has drained.
/harness-heal checks whether a pre-approved, reversible fix (a capture re-run) is safe right now. Propose-only: it applies nothing yet.
When a scheduled run fails, /harness-review explains why and gives you ranked fix options, from a hardened run that can't touch anything but its own note.
/harness-fix records your call on each review: accept puts the fix at the top of the dev queue, decline stops it coming back.
Your memories now join the knowledge graph: the wikilinks you write between memory files become graph edges, with no model and no API cost.
Run python scripts/memory_reachability.py to see which of your saved memories you could not actually find again, and why.
Keeps MEMORY.md small enough to be read in full: only your pickups and what's due now stay loaded, everything else moves to a searchable catalog, with a 16 KB ceiling.
Your read-first Pickups list stays short: finished or long-quiet items are proposed for archive, and quiet ones move to the commitments register instead of disappearing.
/score-vault no longer reports memories as orphans when they are linked by [[wikilink]] or through a sub-index of a sub-index.
Tests that keep the MEMORY.md working set honest: run python scripts/test_memory_working_set.py.
